title: inference-request-forensics-console-showcase-verdantcare
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a console-focused deep dive for VerdantCare's infra and ML teams. Covered request tracing, error analysis, log stitching, and debugging flows. Customer cares about PII handling, VPC private deployment, and latency cost tradeoffs. Agreed to run a 48-hour trace replay pilot and share SOC2 + network diagram.
next_steps: Redwood: share SOC2 + network diagram by 2025-06-02
VerdantCare: provide sample low-sensitivity trace set for 48h replay
Schedule 48h replay kickoff for week of 2025-06-09
action_items: Evan Morales - send security whitepaper and SOC2 link - 2025-06-02
Priya Nair - configure trial trace replay workspace and seed with sample traces - 2025-06-06
Lena Ortiz - export 48h anonymized request logs and upload to shared bucket - 2025-06-04
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 min (approx)
Attendees: Evan Morales, Priya Nair, Jonah Lee - Redwood; Lena Ortiz, Marcus Feld, Jia Chen, Tom Raines - VerdantCare

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of Console request forensics, emphasis on trace playback, stitching logs and error triage flows.

00:00 - Evan Morales: Alright hello everybody, thanks for joining. we have about 50 minutes. i'm Evan, AE for Redwood Inference, with Priya our solutions engineer. quick intros?
00:15 - Lena Ortiz: hi i'm lena, head of ml at VerdantCare, we own the models inside the patient-assist product.
00:23 - Marcus Feld: Marcus here, SRE, i'll be driving the data side and network questions.
00:31 - Jia Chen: Jia, product, focusing on SLA and UX.
00:36 - Priya Nair: great, i'll do the console tour and live playback. fair call — we want to focus on request-level tracing and debugging flows you mentioned in your note.
00:46 - Evan Morales: just to call out success criteria from your RFP: sub-150ms P95 on short prompt path, audit logs for 12 months, and ability to run in a VPC or private deployment. is that right?
01:02 - Lena Ortiz: yes, and also we need deterministic replay for triage and for audits - the ability to stitch logs back to a user session is big for us.
01:12 - Tom Raines: also interested in fallback behavior when a dedicated pool is overloaded - whats the latency hit if it falls back to hosted?
01:25 - Priya Nair: good q. we'll show routing policies and the trace that shows fallbacks. quick note, some of the names in the console export can look a bit off, like "RedWood Console" in older builds, ignore that if you see it.
01:38 - Jonah Lee: i'll send the slides after. Priya, take it away.

03:02 - Priya Nair: okay sharing screen. starting at the Console > Requests page. here you can filter by model, route, or request id. i'm going to pull a recent patient-assist request that had an error. you'll see the request timeline on the right, and the raw payload / embeddings metadata below.
03:25 - Priya Nair: notice the top shows an initial tokenization step, an embedding call to our vector service, then the generation stage. we include ttfb and per-segment latencies.
03:49 - Marcus Feld: is that the KV cash — i mean KV cache — latency showing? sometimes our logs show weird spelling.
03:56 - Priya Nair: yeah that's the KV cache. the console stores both prefix cache hits and KV cache metrics; if a kvcache miss happens we show the fallback to full decode which adds 30-40ms typically.
04:12 - Jia Chen: can you show an example of a request that hit a model variant fallback?
04:18 - Priya Nair: sure. filtering for status code 200 with fallback flag. here's one — you can see the route router selected a smaller-quantized variant and then re-routed to hosted after a brief queue spike. the trace shows an automatic reroute at 00:00:05.
04:35 - Lena Ortiz: do you keep the original prompt in the trace? we need to be careful with PII.
04:42 - Evan Morales: by default we redact PII fields in the request viewer but you can opt-in to keep full payloads in a private deployment; those remain customer-owned and encrypted with their KMS. we'll show the settings shortly.
04:56 - Marcus Feld: encryption at rest and KMS integration is critical. can you produce an audit log for every time a decrypted payload was accessed?
05:02 - Priya Nair: yes audit logs include access events, and the Console exposes a queryable audit table. we also stream to your SIEM if you want.

06:20 - Priya Nair: switching to Request Playback. this is where we take a request id and replay through the serving runtime for debugging. i'm going to replay a 48-hour segment we captured — note we did a light anonymization.
06:38 - Priya Nair: starting replay... you can see step-by-step token ids and model logits if you enable that mode. it's heavy so usually only on internal trial workspaces.
06:52 - Tom Raines: what's the compute cost of a replay like that?
06:58 - Priya Nair: depends on total tokens; we bill a replay run as compute time against a trial quota and typically suggest a short window first. our Optimize tool can estimate costs up front.
07:12 - Lena Ortiz: ok, show us an error case end-to-end where we trace from a user session to the model output that was wrong.
07:20 - Priya Nair: pulling request id VC-err-2025-0420... first the timeline: at 00:00:03 we got a KV cache miss then a fallback to quantized-xxl which had a known regression in prompt alignment. the error is visible in the "diff output" panel where we store model outputs and the matching reference.
07:42 - Priya Nair: note the speech-to-text of the transcript sometimes mangles punctuation, so watch the original payload. sometimes tokens are tokenized differently, that causes subtle differences.
07:55 - Marcus Feld: can we attach our own logs? e.g., application logs that show the user clicked 'submit' at 12:01:22?
08:01 - Priya Nair: yes you can upload or forward your app logs to the console and we do log-stitching based on common keys like session_id or request_id. i'll do a demo of that now.
08:18 - Priya Nair: dropping in a sample app log, filter by session_id=abc123, and you can see requests lined up with the app events.
08:35 - Jia Chen: nice. if we have multiple microservices emitting different trace ids, can the console correlate?
08:42 - Priya Nair: we use probabilistic stitching if direct keys absent; it's not perfect but for most customers it's sufficient to build a timeline. we also support OpenTelemetry context propagation which is the most accurate method.

10:00 - Jonah Lee: quick interjection — we often see customers confuse replay with live inference; replay runs in an isolated sandbox, it doesn't affect production pools.
10:12 - Tom Raines: what about stateful models with KV caches? replay should surface cache state.
10:20 - Priya Nair: good catch. our replay engine can optionally seed KV cache snapshots at selected points, so you can reproduce a hot-cache vs cold-cache scenario. it's a manual flag in the replay UI.

12:45 - Priya Nair: moving on: Error Analysis view. this aggregates failure classes: timeouts, model exceptions, truncated outputs. clicking a cluster shows example traces.
13:02 - Priya Nair: here's a cluster for "truncated outputs" — you can inspect model logits in the debug pane and see an abrupt EOS token. sometimes that's because of bad prompt formatting, sometimes a model bug.
13:25 - Lena Ortiz: can we configure alerts when truncated outputs exceed threshold for a business-critical route?
13:30 - Evan Morales: yes, you can plug alerts into Slack or PagerDuty and tie them to per-route SLOs. we also have anomaly detection that flags sudden regressions.

15:10 - Marcus Feld: on networking: if we run Private (VPC) deployment, how does request telemetry get to Redwood console? we're under strict egress rules.
15:20 - Evan Morales: in Private deployments we ship a control-plane agent that only sends metadata and aggregated telemetry — full payloads never leave your VPC unless you opt in. we also support an on-prem bundle where the control plane runs inside your network.
15:39 - Marcus Feld: will we still get Console features like request playback?
15:44 - Priya Nair: yes, playback runs on your private infra in that case; we provide a management plane that orchestrates the replay but it can be configured to run on customer hosts.

18:05 - Priya Nair: demoing a live root-cause hunt: filter for failed requests in the last 24h for model=patient-assist-v2, severity=error. here's a pattern where failures coincide with a regional GPU flake. you can expand the trace to see the sequence: queue wait -> worker timeout -> fallback to hosted -> success but with increased latency and context loss.
18:30 - Jia Chen: so in the UI we get a request heatmap and we can zoom to the minute. do you persist full per-token logs for 12 months?
18:38 - Priya Nair: per-token logs are expensive; by default we keep request metadata and diffs for 90 days. for audit packages you can enable extended retention and export to your cold storage. those are part of the enterprise package.

20:05 - Evan Morales: quick pause for questions from legal/compliance POV — Lena you mentioned PII and retention. any legal constraints we should be aware of?
20:14 - Lena Ortiz: our data privacy team requires that PII be hashed or removed before leaving our network. also need ability to produce an audit trail if regulators ask for an access report.
20:25 - Evan Morales: understood. we'll share our SOC2 report and an example retention policy soon.

22:40 - Priya Nair: now i want to show a debugging flow: find a bad output -> pull playback -> seed cache snapshot -> rerun with different quantization profiles from Optimize -> compare diffs.
22:55 - Priya Nair: first i clone the request, change the target model to quantized-8bit-pro, check the prompt, and run a dry replay. the compare pane shows token-level diff and a high-level similarity score.
23:18 - Marcus Feld: can we run A/B replays at scale to compare two models across a sample set?
23:25 - Priya Nair: yes, our batch replay supports A/B across a dataset, and we provide aggregated metrics like semantic-similarity, exact-match, and token-coverage. results export as CSV or to your metrics sink.

26:40 - Jia Chen: whats the developer workflow to integrate these traces into our issue tracker? we want quick links in JIRA incidents.
26:50 - Priya Nair: every trace has a permalink and we expose a web hook so you can auto-create issues with context. also manual copy-paste link works.

29:05 - Evan Morales: i want to surface a common cost/latency tradeoff we see: aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency. Optimize offers suggestions per route. Priya, show an optimize suggestion.
29:22 - Priya Nair: here's Optimize: for route patient-assist-short, the suggestion is to enable prefix-cache with 30% hit-rate expected, retarget quantization to 8-bit, and set max-batch-ms to 12ms. projected cost reduction 27% and P95 latency increase 12ms.
29:48 - Lena Ortiz: that's compelling. how accurate are those projections?
29:53 - Priya Nair: they are based on historical distributions; typically within ±10% on cost, ±15ms on latency, but we recommend running a staging benchmark to validate.

32:15 - Tom Raines: what about model governance — we want to pin model versions and have automatic rollback on quality regressions.
32:24 - Evan Morales: rollouts are first-class; you can do canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a previous pinned version if quality or latency SLOs degrade. we tie rollouts to evals so you can gate by performance on a test prompt set.

34:02 - Priya Nair: demoing an automated rollback: we set a canary at 10% traffic, define a metric threshold (semantic-similarity drop > 3%), and the system will rollback and notify via webhook. here, an example we simulated earlier.

36:10 - Marcus Feld: on the topic of observability retention, where do logs go? can we send raw telemetry to our Splunk?
36:18 - Priya Nair: yes, we support forwarders to Splunk, Datadog, and S3. for VPC deployments we can ship a forwarder inside the network.

38:40 - Jia Chen: curious about multi-region failover. if a GPU cluster in us-west degrades, how fast is fallback to eu-west?
38:50 - Priya Nair: routing policy defines region fallback; from our telemetry typical failover is sub-second for routing but you'll see higher TTFB due to cross-region hop, often 50-120ms additional. you can define regional affinity to avoid cross-region fallback for low-latency routes.

41:05 - Priya Nair: last demo: building a runbook in Console. you can capture a sequence of queries that analysts can run when a specific signature occurs. i'll open an example runbook for 'high truncation rate'.
41:22 - Priya Nair: runbook steps: query error cluster -> launch playback on example request -> seed cache snapshot -> run A/B replay -> open issue template -> attach relevant logs. you can schedule runbooks to run automatically on alerts.

44:00 - Lena Ortiz: overall this looks promising. question on licensing: how does billing work for Private vs Hosted?
44:08 - Evan Morales: hosted is usage-based per token/embedding plus retention. Private has a platform fee + reserved capacity for Dedicated pools. we can share a pricing sheet after the call; for pilot we typically offer credits.

46:15 - Tom Raines: about the 48h replay pilot — what's needed from our side for network and access?
46:22 - Priya Nair: we need a sample anonymized trace file in S3 (or a signed URL) and an IAM role for Redwood to read it OR you can upload into the trial workspace. If Private deployment, we'll run the replay in your infra with an agent.
46:40 - Lena Ortiz: we prefer on-prem replay in our staging cluster behind firewall. is that supported?
46:47 - Evan Morales: yes, that's supported. we'll coordinate with your infra team for an on-prem agent.

48:10 - Jonah Lee: quick demo note — sometimes the transcript exporter leaves odd punctuation and token labels. that's the automated ASR; don't rely on it for exact text.
48:25 - Jia Chen: small question: can we obfuscate PHI yet preserve enough context for debugging?
48:33 - Priya Nair: yes, we have a redaction pipeline that can pseudonymize names but keep structure. it's tunable.

50:00 - Evan Morales: alright let's do a quick recap and next steps.
50:06 - Evan Morales: recap: Priya demoed request playback, log stitching, replay with cache seeding, Optimize suggestions, and runbooks. Compliance and private deployment supported. action items: Evan will send SOC2 and network diagram; Priya will provision trial replay workspace; VerdantCare will share anonymized 48h trace.
50:36 - Lena Ortiz: sounds good. we'll aim to get traces to you by 2025-06-04.
50:42 - Evan Morales: great, we'll follow up with scheduling for the week of 2025-06-09. thanks everyone.
50:50 - Tom Raines: thanks all.
50:52 - Meeting end.
